articles.title: Close to where Xi hosted Trump days ago, Chinese bazaar openly sells banned Nvidia chips: Report
articles.summary: Just miles from the villa where US President Donald Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping last week for APEC Summit, some of America's most tightly
articles.body: Just miles from the villa where US President Donald Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping last week for APEC Summit, some of America's most tightly restricted AI chips are being openly sold in Shenzhen's bustling electronics market, according to a Washington Post report.The revelation comes amid heightened US scrutiny of Nvidia following reports that its CEO, Jensen Huang, had an extramarital affair with Alice Huang, a company customer who was allegedly a Chinese intelligence asset.The American newspaper found that vendors at the market were offering some of Nvidia's most advanced chips, including the Blackwell B300, despite US restrictions on their export to China.During a recent visit, one vendor quoted 20 million yuan, or around $3 million, for a server containing eight Blackwell B300 chips after contacting suppliers. Other traders quoted prices ranging from $3 million to $3.4 million for similar servers.The prices have risen sharply in recent weeks amid tighter US export controls. A vendor identified only by his surname, Wu, told The Washington Post that a Blackwell B300 server cost around $2 million two months ago.Nvidia does not publicly disclose prices for its high-end chips.However, an equivalent B300 server costs roughly $500,000 to $600,000 in the US, Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution, told Washington Post.The availability of these chips in Shenzhen highlights the challenges Washington faces in enforcing restrictions aimed at preventing China from accessing advanced American technology and maintaining the US lead in artificial intelligence.Since Nvidia introduced its Blackwell series in 2024, the US has prohibited their shipment to China over national security concerns.These chips generally considered of advanced AI processors that the US restricts from being exported to major powers such as China.However, vendors told The Washington Post that restricted chips continue to reach the Chinese market through supply networks involving Hong Kong and other locations.“If I ever wanted to be a big [Chinese AI developer] and I needed a bunch of Blackwells, I would just go to Huaqiangbei and work out a deal,” Joshua Woodard, founder of Shenzhen-based supply chain consultancy Sparrows, told the newspaper.The market attracts start-ups, independent developers and foreign buyers. One vendor, Jason Cheng, said customers from Russia and Iran had been purchasing Nvidia chips from his stall for the past four or five years.“We don’t care which country a customer comes from, as long as they can pay,” Cheng said.Some traders said the products were kept in warehouses in Shenzhen and nearby Hong Kong and demanded advance deposits before allowing buyers to inspect them.Other Nvidia products, including RTX 5090 and RTX PRO 6000 chips, were openly displayed at the market. A vendor said these were usually sourced through Hong Kong and acknowledged their restricted status.In a statement to Washington Post, Chinese embassy spokesperson Liu Chang said, “China’s position on US chip exports to China is consistent. China opposes the US overstretching the concept of national security and abusing export control measures, which disrupt the stability of global industrial and supply chains.”The report also pointed to public procurement records showing that Chinese research institutes and universities continued to acquire export-restricted Nvidia chips through 2025 and 2026, including as recently as last month.Amid the scandal, Jensen Huang stepped down as Nvidia CEO but returned to the position just days later.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: LMIL unlocks commercial launch of radiation-free breast cancer screening device with official manufacturing license
articles.summary: Access to early breast cancer screening remains an important part of strengthening preventive healthcare, particularly as affordability and reach continue
articles.body: Access to early breast cancer screening remains an important part of strengthening preventive healthcare, particularly as affordability and reach continue to shape screening adoption. In a development aimed at addressing this need, Lord’s Mark Industries Limited has secured a manufacturing licence for its proprietary, radiation-free breast cancer screening technology, marking its second major medical device to enter the market after its AI-enabled dialysis machine. With a proposed screening cost of no more than ₹700 per test, the company plans to expand access to screening through a scalable network across India. The technology is designed for first-line breast cancer screening, including for women with dense breast tissue, with results intended to guide further confirmatory diagnostic investigations and subsequent treatment decisions.The company's LordsMed Breast Cancer Screening Kit uses a wearable system embedded with 28–36 thermal sensors to measure breast surface temperature patterns and identify variations that may indicate underlying biophysical abnormalities. Offering a non-invasive, radiation-free approach, the technology represents a differentiated addition to India's medical technology ecosystem. The company has received manufacturing license number MFG/MD/2026/000736 under Form MD-5 of the Medical Devices Rules, 2017, authorising manufacture for sale or distribution of the Class B medical device.The development comes amid a growing need to strengthen breast cancer screening infrastructure. According to the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), India recorded an estimated 237,231 new breast cancer cases in 2024, highlighting the importance of improving screening access and encouraging timely medical evaluation1.The Indian market is also witnessing significant transformation. According to Grand View Research1 report, India Breast Cancer Diagnostics Market Size & Outlook, The India breast cancer diagnostics market generated a revenue of USD 179.7 million in 2025 and is expected to reach USD 419.1 million by 2033, The India market is expected to grow at a CAGR of 11.4% from 2026 to 2033. The report highlights the increasing role of innovation, precision-led healthcare and advanced diagnostics in shaping the future of breast cancer management. Against this backdrop, Lord’s Mark entry into the screening segment brings an important focus on accessibility and affordable preventive healthcare.The company plans to commence screening services through its own Lord’s path Labs from January 2027 and establish partnerships with private hospitals, diagnostic laboratories and healthcare institutions for wider deployment. Lord’s Mark also intends to explore integration with government healthcare schemes to extend screening services to women across different socio-economic segments. Its proposed pricing of under ₹700 per test is aimed at reducing affordability barriers and encouraging greater participation in preventive screening.Commenting on the development, Dr. Sachidanand Upadhyay, Founder, Managing Director and CEO, Lord’s Mark Industries Limited, said:"At Lord’s Mark Industries, we believe that the true value of healthcare innovation lies in making it accessible to those who need it most. Breast cancer continues to be a major healthcare challenge, and improving access to screening is an essential step towards addressing it. Our radiation-free screening technology reflects our commitment to indigenous innovation with a meaningful social impact. By targeting an affordable price point and building partnerships across government healthcare programs, hospitals and diagnostic networks, we aim to take screening to a much larger population. Our vision is to make early screening more accessible, encourage timely medical intervention and contribute towards a healthier future for women across India."Following the introduction of its AI-enabled dialysis machine, the breast cancer screening kit marks Lord’s Mark next major medical device offering to enter the market. articles.title: 'Mann ka na ho toh jyada acha hai': Piyush Goyal quotes poet Harivansh Bachchan on tariff chaos, India-US trade deal
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Invoking Harivansh Rai Bachchan's poetry, Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal on Friday said the India-US trade deal was nearing
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Invoking Harivansh Rai Bachchan's poetry, Union commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal on Friday said the India-US trade deal was nearing finalisation, with the roadmap and process for concluding the agreement beginning to take shape."The US trade deal is close to culmination. The process and pathway, which was always something that held back finalising the deal, is now taking some shape..." Goyal said while addressing the India Debt Capital Market Summit 2026 virtually.Quoting Bachchan's philosophy, Goyal said the trade disruptions were not what India had wanted, but the country had managed to turn the situation to its advantage."In a way you ask me, it reminds me of Harivansh Rai Bachchan's poetry. Today is his birth anniversary. And Sri Harivansh Rai Bachchan ji had said, Mann ka ho acha, Mann ka ho jyada acha (If things go my way, that's good; if they don't, that's even better). We didn't want all of these things in the world. It was not what we desired," the minister said."But still we converted whatever happened to an advantage to the India growth story, to a sustainable growth story that I think will hold you and all of us in the country, 1.4 billion Indians in good stead in the years to come," he said."Ultimately what matters is our ability to counter whatever situation comes our way," he added.Goyal's remarks come amid renewed trade uncertainty after the US Trade Representative (USTR) proposed duties of up to 25% on Indian goods under a Section 301 investigation into alleged structural excess capacity in manufacturing.Washington has indicated that the proposed tariff rate could be reduced to 17% if India reaches a reciprocal trade agreement addressing the findings of the investigation.Goyal also said the India-European Union free trade agreement (FTA) was expected to be signed later this year and could come into effect by March or April 2027."The EU FTA will hopefully be executed and signed later this year and come into effect by March or April next year," he added.Over the past five years, India has finalised nine FTAs covering 38 developed countries, providing preferential access to markets with a combined GDP of $70 trillion.Another eight to nine agreements currently under negotiation could expand India's market access to economies worth $85 trillion, he said.Goyal stated that India's economy had continued to grow despite global headwinds, including geopolitical conflicts, oil price volatility and tariff-related disruptions."Despite all of these uncertainties around the world, I think the one thing that remained constant was the world's trust in the India growth story. And we delivered on that trust," he said.India recorded 7.8% growth in the first quarter of the current financial year, with Goyal expressing confidence that the momentum would continue in the September quarter.Gross fixed capital formation grew by around 12 per cent, while bank credit expanded by nearly 19 per cent, reflecting continued investment and economic activity, he said.Exports stood at around $570 billion in the first seven months of the financial year, while October exports touched a record nearly $90 billion, putting India on track to meet its $1 trillion annual export target."I think we are well on track to achieve our USD 1 trillion target," Goyal said, crediting exporters, manufacturers, service providers and those in the agriculture and fisheries sectors for the growth.India has maintained that trade-related concerns should be resolved through ongoing bilateral negotiations with the US and said it was examining the latest notice issued by the US Trade Representative (USTR).New Delhi has rejected Washington's allegations of structural excess capacity in manufacturing and said it would work towards an early conclusion of the bilateral trade agreement (BTA)."India and the US are engaged in negotiations for a BTA. It has been India’s position that any trade-related concerns should be addressed within the framework of these negotiations," the government had earlier said on Wednesday.The first Section 301 investigation is already facing a legal challenge in the US, while the latest action is also likely to be challenged in American courts.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: For Nike, a comeback is a marathon and not a sprint
articles.summary: Nike CEO Elliott Hill is clear-eyed about his company’s problems, bluntly telling a packed room at the company’s first investor event in a decade: “We’re not where we want to be.”
articles.body: Nike CEO Elliott Hill is clear-eyed about his company’s problems, bluntly telling a packed room at the company’s first investor event in a decade: “We’re not where we want to be.” Nike, the company behind the iconic “Just Do It” slogan, Air Jordan and other trailblazing shoes that changed distance running, was once the envy of the athletic footwear and apparel industry. Now, it’s rolling out a comeback plan as the stock hovers at a 13-year low and the company is steeped in a several-year streak of flat or declining sales as consumers switch to trendier sportswear brands. Employees are also bracing for another wave of layoffs next year, marking the fourth round since Hill took the top job in 2024. Nike’s problems are largely “self-inflicted,” according to Joseph Civello, a research analyst for Truist Securities, pointing toward its strategy shift a few years ago under its previous CEO. Nike began selling its shoes and apparel on its own website and stores rather than relying on outside retailers. (Hill has reversed those plans.) “That led them to a very complacent state, where they were launching the same product over and over again, and weren’t really innovating,” he told CNN, adding that since Nike was no longer close to its retail partners, it was slow to notice sales slipping. The problem was masked, he said, because “the same old Jordans were selling extremely well.” With Nike absent from the shelves at traditional retailers, sales of smaller competitors surged, like Brooks Running, On or Salomon. While those brands are still “ankle biters” in terms of market share compared to Nike, Civello doesn’t expect them to give up those gains as they’ve innovated well and tapped into social media to reach consumers. Still, Hill is optimistic about the future of the world’s largest sportswear company. “We have a growing market, more ways to serve athletes and advantages built over decades,” he said. The plan Nike’s plan focuses on improving innovation and strengthening relationships with individual athletes and communities, such as a newly inked deal with Formula 1. It’s also developing a faster supply chain to be more responsive to trends. The company will also emphasize products for performance sports, like running, training and basketball, as well as reimagining its products from its Nike Sportswear, Jordan and Converse brands. However, Nike says any benefit from the turnaround is years away. Nike forecasts revenue will stay flat or even decline for another two years before growth returns. The company then expects $5 billion in additional revenue by 2031 from improvements in its performance sports and sportswear brands. “We’re getting the marketplace back to a healthier position,” Hill said. “Much of the pressure that we face comes from a handful of classic footwear franchises coming down from their peak.” Collective sales of its franchise shoes like Nike’s Air Jordan 1, Air Force 1 and Converse’s Chuck Taylors have fallen about 50% in the past few years, from $13 billion in 2024 to a projected $6 billion next year. “Clearly, this is a significant headwind to our business,” said Chief Financial Officer Dave Denton. “And, importantly, it’s taught us a lesson about the downside of being over reliant on a few key products.” For the Jordan brand, that means reducing the number of shoes Nike sells to make the brand feel special again. Hill said the company will also strengthen its “position in the cities and the communities that shape basketball and street culture” to compete with New Balance and Skechers. Converse, which has been rumored in recent months to be on the block, will also be repositioned to focus on its connection with Chuck Taylor and Jack Purcell’s original designs. The company’s overseas business is also getting a reset. Nike’s business in China has sputtered, with sales falling from about $8 billion in 2021 to $6 billion this year as customers turn to domestic Chinese brands like Anta and Li-Ning. Nike also hasn’t kept up with popular livestream shopping networks that flog their competitor’s products. In response, Nike will design more of its designs within the country and increase its live streaming. “Local competitors are moving with speed and fluency,” said Cathy Sparks, Nike’s vice president and general manager of its China business. “Our marketplace and our model have not kept pace and our results show it.” India, however, is a bright spot. Nike expects to triple its business there in the next five years with an emphasis on running, training and new cricket gear ahead of the sport’s return to the 2028 summer Olympics. Will it work? Not everyone is convinced the plan will succeed. For Truist’s Civello, Nike’s targets are more optimistic than he’d hoped for, especially since it expects a few more years of sales struggles. “Who knows what’s going to be popular in five years?” he said. “It’s a lot to say that a brand as big as Nike that has had the problems it’s had for the past few years can outpace the market in terms of growth.” Plus, the onslaught of competitors isn’t expected to cool down either, added Neil Saunders, managing director of GlobalData Retail. “There’s a lot of skepticism over whether Nike can course correct, and that’s underpinned by a view that it may have to accept that its market share will never get back to previous heights because the trading and competitive environment is so different than it once was,” he told CNN. Wall Street shares that skepticism. Nike shares fell after Hill’s plans were revealed, but have since rebounded. The stock is down more than 40% since the beginning of the year. Hill believes the “strength is already inside Nike. Now is the time to unleash our full potential.”

Nike's plan focuses on improving innovation and strengthening relationships with individual athletes and communities, such as a newly inked deal with Formula 1. It's also developing a faster supply chain to be more responsive to trends.

The company will also emphasize products for performance sports, like running, training and basketball, as well as reimagining its products from its Nike Sportswear, Jordan and Converse brands.

However, Nike says any benefit from the turnaround is years away.

Nike forecasts revenue will stay flat or even decline for another two years before growth returns. The company then expects $5 billion in additional revenue by 2031 from improvements in its performance sports and sportswear brands.

articles.title: It’s up to Congress to clean up the country’s prediction-market mess
articles.summary: Congress should stop letting prosecutors and appeals courts guess what it meant and say what it wants.
articles.body:
In the space of just eight days last month, the fight over sports “prediction markets” stopped being a regulatory dispute and became something closer to a constitutional standoff.

On Oct. 20, Utah sued Kalshi and two Susquehanna market-making firms in state court, alleging that Kalshi’s sports contracts constitute illegal gambling. On Oct. 26, the U.S. and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission sued Utah in federal court — the 10th state the agency has taken on.

Two days later, Utah’s attorney general filed criminal charges against KalshiEX and its two co-founders, CEO Tarek Mansour and COO Luana Lopes Lara: 12 felony counts of online gambling promotion, a second-degree felony count of pattern of unlawful activity and a misdemeanor, built on wagers an undercover agent placed on football and other games.

“Calling it a ‘prediction market’ doesn’t change what it is, and being federally registered doesn’t put a company above the law,” Utah Attorney General Derek Brown said. Kalshi called the charges “ a crazy overreach .” Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chairman Michael Selig said that Congress made his agency “ the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets .”

Each side says Congress has already decided. The trouble is that the law they are fighting over, the 2010 Dodd-Frank Act , was written years before anyone was trading NFL spreads on a federally registered exchange.

Congress must stop letting prosecutors and appeals courts guess what it meant and instead state its own clear meaning.

The courts cannot agree. In April, a divided Third Circuit panel sided with Kalshi against New Jersey. In August, the Ninth Circuit ruled for Nevada. A federal judge in Utah ruled in August that the state’s gambling laws apply, and the Tenth Circuit refused to pause that ruling. Yet in Arizona, a federal judge blocked the state’s criminal case against Kalshi at the feds’ request. On Nov. 3, the Second Circuit declined to shield Kalshi and Coinbase from New York and Connecticut while their appeals continue. AskSpinner News tracks this litigation , and the map keeps getting more crowded, not less.

New Jersey has asked the Supreme Court to take on the question, in Flaherty v. KalshiEX ; Kalshi’s response is due Dec. 7. Ohio and 38 other states , plus the District of Columbia, have filed in support of New Jersey . So have former Sen. Christopher Dodd (D-Conn.), one of the law’s namesakes, and former Commodity Futures Trading Commission Chairman Gary Gensler .

When the people who wrote and implemented a statute are filing amicus briefs about what it means, the statute is no longer doing its job.

Even a Supreme Court ruling would settle less than it seems. The justices can tell us whether Dodd-Frank preempts state gambling law, but they cannot write the rules a sports-betting market needs. Today the answer to basic consumer-protection questions depends on which label wins.

Most states bar sports betting under 21; Kalshi accepts users from 18, a gap the American Gaming Association highlighted in its Supreme Court brief , citing a CNN estimate that 18- to 20-year-olds had traded about $5.4 billion on the platform by late August. Self-exclusion lists, advertising limits and problem-gambling funding are all built around state licenses. A preemption ruling either sweeps those away for one class of company or strands a federally registered industry in 50 different legal regimes.

Congress can fix this with a short bill. It should decide, explicitly, whether contracts on the outcome of sporting events listed on registered exchanges are swaps under the Commodity Exchange Act.

If Congress says no, it should give exchanges a defined wind-down period, so that the transition happens on a timetable rather than through criminal summonses issued to executives.

If Congress says yes, it should attach a federal floor that matches what bettors get from state regulators: a minimum age of 21 for sports contracts, participation in state self-exclusion lists, advertising standards and a funding stream for problem-gambling services. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission was built to police manipulation and counterparty risk, not gambling harm, and it should not have to improvise those rules.

Either answer is defensible. What is not defensible is the current approach: a federal agency suing 10 states, a state charging company founders with felonies over conduct a federal regulator calls lawful, and customers whose protections depend on their ZIP code.

A federal judge in Salt Lake City heard the Commodity Futures Trading Commission’s emergency motion against Utah on Nov. 20 without ruling from the bench. Congress does not need to wait for a court ruling, or for the Supreme Court, to do its job.

Kimi Yu is the founder and CEO of AskSpinner, a global gambling industry platform covering industry insight and regulatory developments.

articles.title: Trump demands GDP data probe as chances of rate hike rise: What to know
articles.summary: President Trump on Thursday pressed for an investigation into gross domestic product (GDP) figures released by the Commerce Department prior to the midterms. “It was just revealed that the REAL Numbers on the Economy, published before the Election, were FAKE, and a correction was issued yesterday by the people in the Government Agency that does…
articles.body:
President Trump on Thursday pressed for an investigation into gross domestic product (GDP) figures released by the Commerce Department prior to the midterms.

“It was just revealed that the REAL Numbers on the Economy, published before the Election, were FAKE, and a correction was issued yesterday by the people in the Government Agency that does these numbers,” Trump wrote in a Truth Social post on Thursday.

“Third Quarter GDP Growth has now been corrected to be 4.3%, instead of 3.4%, a major difference! Why wasn’t the correct number issued before the Election? I am asking for an immediate investigation of this situation. This is not a small error, this is a massive, and purposeful, error,” he added.

BestReviews is reader-supported and may earn an affiliate commission.

Trump also mentioned the correction, which is not unusual, in a long-winded Thanksgiving post later in the morning.

Here’s what you need to know about Trump’s complaints and the GDP data released by his own administration:

Latest battle in Trump’s fight against official data

The pace of economic growth reported by the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Economic Analysis on Wednesday was the fastest in three years.

The sharp revision — from 3.4 percent to 4.3 percent in the period from July to September — was also well above expectations from economists.

Trump’s complaints about federal economic data are not new.

In August 2025, the president ordered his team to fire the commissioner of the Bureau of Labor Statistics in the wake of a dour jobs report he specifically blamed on the appointee of former President Biden.

Trump said on Truth Social at the time that the commissioner, Erika McEntarfer, “faked the jobs numbers” prior to the 2024 election to bolster former Vice President Kamala Harris’s campaign for the White House.

Trump also called federal unemployment figures “totally fiction” even after his election in 2016.

Growth figures boost chances of interest rate hike

The escalating pace of economic growth is contributing to the near certainty that the Federal Reserve will once again increase borrowing rates when it meets again next month.

“It is more urgent than ever that Fed officials step up the pace of interest rate hikes to cool off economic demand,” Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at Fwdbonds, told Reuters . “It was once thought that import tariffs and energy prices from the Mideast war were one-off factors behind the higher inflation numbers, but increasingly the inflation fires look to be stoked by old-fashioned economic demand pressures.”

Jim Baird of Plante Moran Financial Advisors told CNBC the data “reinforces an increasingly familiar tension” that the economy is “performing quite well, but its resilience also gives the Fed an even stronger case for further rate hikes.”

Traders have nearly 100 percent confidence the Federal Open Market Committee will increase interest rates in December, according to the CME FedWatch tool .

The state of the economy was central to this year’s midterms, with Democrats retaking the House and Senate with campaigns centered around affordability.

Most voters said that Trump’s policies had hindered growth and driven up costs, according to The AP Voter Poll .

About two-thirds of voters said Trump was responsible for fueling inflation, compared with about half who held the same view of then-President Biden during the 2022 midterms.

According to a survey conducted before Election Day, the rising cost of living and dissatisfaction with the president were the top concerns for nearly half of voters.

While the latest GDP revision shows robust economic growth, it only adds to concerns about inflation risks.

articles.title: Trump to visit groundbreaking for semiconductor manufacturer that supplies Nvidia: Reports

articles.body:
President Trump is reportedly set to attend the groundbreaking of a Phoenix facility that will manufacture semiconductor chips, including for Nvidia, which has seized the spotlight this month over the ouster and reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang.

A White House official told multiple outlets that Trump will tour and deliver remarks at a Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) plant on Dec. 4.

TSMC unveiled plans to expand into Arizona in 2020, saying at the time it would spend roughly $12 billion from 2021-29 on the project.

The Hill has reached out to the White House and TSMC for comment.

Trump’s visit will come following Nvidia’s reinstatement of Huang as CEO after the president’s urging .

In announcing the reinstatement of Huang, who resigned on Nov. 12 amid reports about his extramarital affairs — including one with an alleged Chinese spy — Nvidia’s board argued his return did not pose any national security risks, citing conversations with “senior levels” of the U.S. government.

“And I must tell you, it was a lot easier to convince them yesterday than it was a week and a half ago,” Trump said of the board on CNBC, referencing Nvidia’s falling stock price.

While Nvidia shares saw a Huang-fueled bump on Monday, they have since declined and closed at $150.49 on Black Friday.

Nvidia’s stock, while above last Friday’s closing mark of $125.53 per share, is nearly $93 below where it stood on Oct. 6 — when it reached an all-time high of $243.37 per share.

Trump did not rule out pardoning Huang on Tuesday, although he told the New York Post he did not think it would be “necessary.”
